title: CITIZENS’ COMMENTS
COMMENTS BY THE CITY COMMISSION, CITY ATTORNEY & CITY MANAGER

minutes_note:
YMCA
Vice Mayor Callari requested the results of the Park East Community Charrette be brought forward so the Commission and residents can be informed about the future use of the old Hollywood Police Department site on Hollywood Boulevard and Park Road. She stated the YMCA had previously expressed interest in a property in the area, and that the site may represent an opportunity to relocate the YMCA facility.
GO Bond Projects
Vice Mayor Callari requested Commission support to look at completing all outstanding GO Bond projects, specifically Rotary Park, which she stated has not yet broken ground despite plans being complete.
Jose Cortes, Assistant City Manager, stated Rotary Park received its final Broward County storm water permit earlier this year and the project is now out for bid. He stated the pricing for multiple options including base drainage design, improved field drainage, and turf options should be returned to the Commission by the August meeting. Jose Cortes, Assistant City Manager, stated the only remaining GO Bond project without a committed contract is the FEC Corridor Project, which has been delayed by Brightline, however, the City Manager has directed staff to move forward.
Utility Box
Vice Mayor Callari thanked City staff for resolving a 14-year complaint from a resident about an improperly placed AT&T utility box on their property. She stated through persistent effort, the box will be relocated within the next six months.
title: Vice Mayor Callari, District 3

minutes_note:
World Cup
Commissioner Gruber stated he could not find the World Cup Block Watch Party events on the City's Facebook nor on the City’s webpage. He requested those events be more prominently promoted.
Mayor Levy stated the events are scheduled for June 27, 2026, for the Colombia game and July 19, 2026, for the final.
Community Garden
Commissioner Gruber stated the Community Garden at Oak Lake Community Center appears to be unused and questioned whether it could be activated as programming for the senior center planned to open at the Oak Lake Community Center in November.
Ball Field
Commissioner Gruber stated a ball field at a park in Lakes of Emerald Hills has been overgrown for many years and requested staff look into restoring it to a usable condition for residents who play kickball, baseball, and softball.
title: Commissioner Gruber, District 4

minutes_note:
Traffic Calming
Commissioner Biederman stated residents in Boulevard Heights are excited about the traffic calming measures being installed along Arthur Street and 76th Avenue.
Commission in the Community
Commissioner Biederman announced a Commission in the Community event on June 24, 2026, at the Boulevard Heights Community Center. The Department of Public Utilities will be present to answer questions about the septic-to-sewer program, along with a "Taste of the West Side" food component.
National Night Out
Commissioner Biederman announced the Driftwood Civic Association is hosting a National Night Out event on August 4, 2026.
Sewer Systems
Commissioner Biederman requested Commission support for staff to evaluate extending the sewer line west to 64th Avenue along Johnson Street to connect commercial properties there to City's sewer system, which he stated would stimulate economic development.
Vice Mayor Callari and Commissioner Quintana supported the request.
Driving Ranges
Commissioner Biederman requested Commission support for staff to evaluate whether City-owned land near Echo Golf Course could host a public driving range. He stated there has been a loss of driving ranges in the City due to the redevelopment of Orangebrook Golf Course and the Hollywood Beach Golf Course.
Commissioner Hernandez and Mayor Levy supported the request.
title: Commissioner Biederman, District 5

minutes_note:
Orangebrook Redevelopment
Commissioner Quintana requested an update on next stages for the Orangebrook redevelopment timeline.
ILA Funds
Commissioner Quintana questioned the current status of the City's Interlocal Agreement (ILA) funds, as she is aware that a significant funding amount remains unspent.
Traffic Calming
Commissioner Quintana requested an update on traffic calming measures at 59th Avenue and Fillmore Street, where multiple accidents have occurred.
Community Cats
Commissioner Quintana stated that she would like to see a public information campaign about the proper way to manage community cats. She explained she has observed residents from outside her neighborhood leaving food on sidewalks, which creates nuisance conditions.
Iguanas
Commissioner Quintana requested a public information campaign about best practices for managing iguanas, which she stated are making a significant comeback since the cold spell.
Recycling and Garbage Bins
Commissioner Quintana stated there was a very successful Storytime in the Park program last Friday. She stated during the event she noticed recycling and garbage bins in parks are not clearly labeled and requested that all parks and public facilities be surveyed to ensure proper labeling on the bins.
World Cup
Commissioner Quintana announced the German American Club is hosting a World Cup watch party this Friday for the U.S. versus Australia match, with doors opening at 2:00 PM and free admission.
Tree Canopy Project
Commissioner Quintana announced a fourth Tree Canopy Project workshop on June 27, 2026, at the Washington Park Community Center. She stated there will be food, art activities for children, and free trees or plants to take home.
Ribbon Cutting
Commissioner Quintana announced that the COVID Memorial ribbon cutting at Bob Butterworth Park is scheduled for July 1, 2026, at 10:00 AM.
title: Commissioner Quintana, District 6

minutes_note:
Hollywood Beach Resort
Commissioner Shuham stated she voted against the Hollywood Beach Resort vested rights resolution and it should not be interpreted as opposition to residential use on the site. She stated she supports residential units there, ideally in combination with a five-star resort and historic preservation and is eager to see the bonus overlay that staff is developing for the area.
Iguana Issue
Commissioner Shuham stated the issue of iguanas undermining City facilities is a long-standing concern and she requested that staff revisit a citywide iguana management plan.
Traffic Calming
Commissioner Shuham stated staff needs to respond to residents’ email regarding traffic calming along Johnson Street. She stated residents are also concerned about traffic calming near the golf course on Polk Street.
Hurricane Preparedness
Commissioner Shuham thanked Veronica Perez, Emergency Manager; Jeff Levy, Fire Chief, and Chris O'Brien, Director of Public Safety, for putting together a well-received hurricane preparedness event at the Beach Community Center on June 11, 2026.
Development Review Process
Commissioner Shuham stated as part of the revisions to the Development Review process, residents’ loss the ability to publicly review projects early. She requested Commission support for posting the Development Review Committee (DRC) agenda be posted a few days or a week before each meeting so that residents can see what development projects are coming.
Commissioner Hernandez and Commissioner Quintana supported the request.
July 4th Celebration
Commissioner Shuham stated she will see everyone at the 4th of July celebration event.
title: Commissioner Shuham, District 1

minutes_note:
Water Meters
Commissioner Hernandez requested Commission support for staff to review the City's practice of estimating water usage for up to 60 days before actually reading a meter. He requested that the trigger for a meter read be tightened.
Vice Mayor Callari and Mayor Levy supported the request.
ILA Funds
Commissioner Hernandez stated he met with Ryan Coote, Director of Housing and Community Development, earlier in the day and that the City currently has approximately $8 to $9 million funding available in ILA funds with $1.2 million encumbered. He stated a $4 million project is expected to come before the Commission on July 7th.
Commissioner Hernandez requested the Commission be mindful of how ILA funds are used to ensure money remains available for homeowner rehabilitation programs for low-to-moderate-income residents.
Traffic Calming
Commissioner Hernandez stated traffic calming on 22nd Avenue from Pembroke to Washington Street and at the Van Buren Street and 24th Avenue intersection should be prioritized.
1980 Grant Street
Commissioner Hernandez stated he would like staff to bring back a broader review of how the planning and variance process applies to warehouse conversions in the regional activity center, using the current application at 1980 Grant Street as the catalyst.
Commissioner Hernandez stated the property received a variance eliminating 11 of 12 required parking spaces without a site plan showing where the one approved space will be located and would like to establish better standards for future warehouse reuse applications.
Andria Wingett, Director of Development Services, stated there will be approximately four meetings to bring it back, after noticing requirements are met. She stated that the applicant needs to be aware, and this would be a de novo hearing.
Commissioner Hernandez stated he has asked for the regional activity center to be reviewed in the past. He stated he wants more information on this project, including the use of the property and site plan. Commissioner Hernandez stated the variance for 11 parking spaces was granted with no information. He stated his intention are to make the project better, not kill it.
Mayor Levy requested clarification from Commissioner Hernandez regarding his request, if it was for the subject, or is he requesting Commission Call for Review (CRR).
Commissioner Hernandez stated he is looking for Commission support for a CRR so that this can be addressed. Vice Mayor Callari supported the request.
Commissioner Biederman questioned the time frame involved in bringing the CRR and if this will delay the project.
Adria Wingett, Director of Development Services, stated there will be approximately four meetings to bring it back a CRR, after noticing requirements are met. She stated that the applicant needs to be aware, and this would be a de novo hearing.
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated the applicant at 1980 Grant Street proposes a craft coffee roasting and entrepreneurial maker space, similar to an operation in Doral. She stated staff required a parking engineer to evaluate the business model and determine that the operation could function with one parking space. Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated the Regional Activity Center zoning explicitly encourages adaptive reuse of warehouse buildings, and Commissioner Hernandez's pilot project to create additional legal on-street parking south of Hollywood Boulevard on 19th Avenue and 20th Avenue addresses the broader parking challenge in the area.
Commissioner Biederman stated he supports the request for a CRR.
title: Commissioner Hernandez, District 2

minutes_note:
World Cup
Mayor Levy stated that he is excited about the World Cup activity in Hollywood and is looking forward to the watch parties and the associated economic activities.
4th of July Event
Mayor Levy requested staff share details about special July 4th and America 250th Anniversary events so that residents can plan to attend.
title: Mayor Levy

minutes_note:
Happy Holiday
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, wished everyone a happy Juneteenth and a happy Fourth of July.
title: City Attorney

minutes_note:
Mango Tango
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced the Hammerstein House is hosting a Mango Tango Festival on Saturday from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, featuring a mango art exhibition, recipe contest, children's art corner, and tango demonstrations. She stated a $5 donation is requested for the Historical Society and free admission for children 12 and under.
Downtown Artwalk
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced the Downtown Hollywood Art Walk from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
Acela Training
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced Development Services will host an in-person and virtual training on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM for residents, property owners, and the business community on how to navigate the new Acela online permitting portal.
Commission Meeting
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced at the July 7, 2026, meeting the Commission will consider the Solid Waste Authority item, and the Solid Waste Authority Executive Committee approved an opt-out option with no conditions, subject to final RFP pricing, with a second opt-out available in 2048.
title: City Manager

The meeting adjourned at 5:42 PM.

Any person wishing to appeal any decision made by this Commission with respect to any matter considered at such meeting or hearing will need a record of the proceedings, and for such purposes may need to ensure that a verbatim record of the proceedings is made, which record includes the testimony and evidence upon which the appeal is made.
Two or more members of the same city board, commission, or committee, who are not of this Commission, may attend this meeting and may, at that time, discuss matters on which foreseeable action may later be taken by their board, commission or committee.
Persons with disabilities who require reasonable accommodations to participate in City programs and/or services may call the Clarissa Ip, ADA Coordinator/City Engineer, five business days in advance at 954-921-3915 (voice) or email: cip@hollywoodfl.org. If an individual is hearing or speech impaired, please call 1-800-955-8771 (V-TDD).
Disclosure of Real Estate Interests and Business Relationships - When an agenda item involves the use or development of land, each member of the City Commission, City Manager, Assistant City Manager(s), City Attorney, Deputy City Attorney, and the director and assistant director (s) of each City department/office shall disclose orally, at the time the City Commission begins to discuss the item, or in writing to the City Clerk prior to the publication of the agenda, any significant interest (as defined below) that such City official or employee or any relative of such City official or employee has in land located within 300 feet of the land that is the subject of the item. When an agenda item involves an invitation for bids, request for proposals, request for qualifications, request for letters of interest, or other competitive solicitation, each member of the City Commission, City Manager, Assistant City Manager(s), City Attorney, Deputy City Attorney, and the director and assistant director (s) of each City department/office shall disclose orally, at the time the City Commission begins to discuss the item, or in writing to the City Clerk prior to the publication of the agenda, any client or business relationship that such City official or employee or any relative of such City official or employee has with any business entity that has submitted a response to the competitive solicitation. “Significant interest” means ownership of more than five percent of the value of the land.
Persons attending meetings shall remain seated at all times unless called upon to speak, will not call out comments during the meeting or make inappropriate hand or facial gestures. Please silence all cell phones prior to entering the meeting.

QUASI-JUDICIAL HEARING PROCEDURES
AND RULES FOR EX-PARTE COMMUNICATIONS
I. Scope and Applicability. These procedures shall apply to all quasi-judicial hearings held by the City Commission or by any Board or Committee (hereinafter referred to as “Boards”) which holds quasi-judicial hearings. The City Attorney shall determine which matters are quasi-judicial in nature and shall direct the City Clerk or Board liaison to designate specially such matters on the agenda.
II. Proceedings. Mayor, Vice Mayor or other presiding officer (hereafter, the "Presiding Officer") shall conduct the proceedings and maintain order. The City Attorney or legal advisor shall represent the City Commission or Board, rule on all evidentiary and procedural issues and objections, and advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and necessary factual findings. Hearings shall be conducted informally, but with decorum. Formal rules of procedure shall not apply except as set forth herein; however, fundamental due process shall be accorded.
III. Unauthorized Communications. In all quasi-judicial hearings, all rulings must be based only upon the evidence presented at the hearing. In accordance with Section 286.0115(1), Florida Statutes, ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members in quasi-judicial matters is permissible and the adherence to the following procedures shall remove the presumption of prejudice arising from ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members:
1. The substance of any ex parte communication with a City Commissioner or Board member which relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board is not presumed prejudicial to the action if the subject of the communication and the identity of the person, group, or entity with whom the communication took place is disclosed and made a part of the record before the final action on the matter.
2. A City Commissioner or Board member may read a written communication from any person. However, a written communication that relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action, and such written communication shall be made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
3. City Commissioners or Board members may conduct investigations and site visits and may receive expert opinions regarding quasi-judicial action pending before them. Such activities shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action if the existence of the investigation, site visit, or expert opinion is made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
4. Disclosure made pursuant to subparagraphs 1, 2 and 3 must be made before or during the public meeting at which a vote is taken on such matters, so that persons who have opinions contrary to those expressed in the ex parte communication are give a reasonable opportunity to refute or respond to the communication.
IV. Witnesses and Supporting Materials. At least eight City business days before a quasi-judicial hearing.
A. Staff shall prepare a report, recommendation and supporting materials, a copy of which shall be available to the applicant, appellant and to the public at the City Clerk’s Office. Included in the supporting materials will be copies of all exhibits and documents upon which staff’s recommendation is based.
B. The Applicant and the Appellant, if applicable, shall submit a detailed outline of the argument in support of their application, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify in support of the application (including resumes for any witness the party intends to qualify as an expert).
C. The eight City business day deadline is necessary to ensure the Commission or Board members are given sufficient opportunity to review the written submissions prior to the hearing, and shall be strictly observed. Should the eight day City business day deadline be missed by either staff or the Applicant, the item may be continued at the discretion of the City Commission or Board to the next available agenda.
V. Party Intervenors. The City Attorney may allow a person to intervene as a Party Intervenor if they meet the following requirements:
A. The person must have an interest in the application, which is different than the public at large.
B. At least three days prior to the hearing, the person shall submit a written request to intervene including: a detailed outline of their interest in the application and argument in favor or against it, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at the hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify on their behalf (including resumes for any witness the person intends to qualify as an expert).
VI. Conduct of Hearing.
A. The Presiding Officer shall call the proceeding to order and announce that the hearing has begun.
B. The Presiding Officer, City Attorney or legal advisor shall inquire whether all parties, members of the public and Commission or Board members agree to waiving the quasi-judicial hearing.
C. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Attorney, legal advisor or Presiding Officer shall explain the rules concerning procedure, testimony, and admission of evidence.
D. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Clerk or staff liaison shall swear in all witnesses who are to testify at the hearing.
E. The order of proof shall be as follows:
1. A representative of the City’s staff (or outside counsel) shall briefly describe the Applicant’s request, introduce and review all relevant exhibits and evidence, report staff’s recommendation, and present any testimony in support of staff’s recommendation. Staff shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make their full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
2. The Appellant, if applicable, (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Appellant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make its full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
3. Any Party Intervenor (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of or opposed to the application. A Party Intervenor shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board Member.
4. The Applicant (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Applicant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
5. Any other persons present who wish to submit relevant information to the City Commission or Board shall speak next for a maximum of three minutes each (excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member). Members of the public will be permitted to present their non-expert opinions, but the Commission or board will be expressly advised that public sentiment is not relevant to the decision, which must be based only upon competent and substantial evidence.
6. The Appellant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
7. The Applicant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
8. The Party Intervenor will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
9. The City’s staff will make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
10. At the discretion of the Presiding Officer, the Applicant may be permitted to respond to the final Party Intervenor and staff comments and recommendations (maximum of three minutes).
G. The City Attorney or legal advisor will advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and the factual findings that must be made to approve or deny the application.
H. The City Commission or Board will conduct open deliberation of the application. The Presiding Officer shall have the discretion to reopen the proceeding for additional testimony or argument by the parties when an outcome substantially different than either the granting or denial of the application is being considered. After deliberations, a vote shall be taken to approve, approve with conditions or deny the application.
VII. Examination by Commissioners and City Attorney or Legal Advisor. Commissioners, Board members and the City Attorney or Legal Advisor may ask questions of persons presenting testimony or evidence at any time during the proceedings until commencement of deliberation.
VIII. Cross-Examination of Witnesses. After each witness testifies, the City staff representative, the Applicant’s representative, Appellant’s representative, and/or the Party Intervenor’s representative shall be permitted to question the witness, but such cross-examination shall be limited to matters about which the witness testified and shall be limited to five minutes per side. Members of the public will not be permitted to cross-examine witnesses. Cross-examination shall be permitted only as would be permitted in a Florida court of law.
IX. Rules of Evidence.
A. All evidence of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs shall be admissible, whether or not such evidence would be admissible in a court of law in Florida. Irrelevant, immaterial, harassing, defamatory or unduly repetitive evidence shall be excluded.
B. Hearsay evidence may be used for the purposes of supplementing or explaining other evidence, but it shall not be sufficient by itself to support a finding unless it would be admissible over objection in a civil action.
C. Documentary evidence may be presented in the form of a copy or the original. Upon request, parties shall be given an opportunity to compare the copy with the original.
X. Statements of Counsel. Statements of counsel, or any non-attorney representative, shall only be considered as argument and not testimony unless counsel or the representative is sworn in and the testimony if based on actual personal knowledge of the matters which are the subject of the statements.
XI. Continuances and Deferrals. The City Commission or Board shall consider requests for continuances made by City staff, the Applicant, the Appellant or a Party Intervenor and may grant continuances in its sole discretion. If, in the opinion of the City Commission or Board, any testimony or documentary evidence or information presented at the hearing justifies allowing additional research or review in order to properly determine the issue presented, then the City Commission or Board may continue the matter to a time certain to allow for such research or review.
XII. Transcription of hearing.
A. The City Clerk or staff liaison shall preserve the official transcript of the hearing through tape recording and/or video recording.
B. the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may arrange, at its own expense, for a court reporter to transcribe the hearing.
C. The Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may request that all or a part of the transcript of a hearing be transcribed into verbatim, written form. In such case, the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor requesting the transcript shall be responsible for the cost of production of the transcription and the transcription shall become the official transcript.
XIII. Maintenance of Evidence and Other Documents. The Office of the City Clerk or staff liaison shall retain all of the evidence and documents presented at the hearing unless any such evidence is too large to be stored by the City Clerk or staff liaison. In that event, such evidence will be stored in the Community Planning and Development Department.
XIV. False Testimony. Any willful false swearing on the part of any witness or person giving evidence before the Commission or Board as to any material fact in the proceedings shall be deemed to be perjury and shall be punished in the manner prescribed by law for such offense.
XV. Failure of Applicant to Appear. If the Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or their representative fails to appear at the time fixed for the hearing, and such absence is not excused by the Commission or Board, the Commission or Board may proceed to hear the evidence and render a decision thereon in absentia.
XVI. Subpoena Power. The Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or City’s staff shall be entitled to compel the attendance of witnesses through the use of subpoenas. All such subpoenas shall be issued by the City Clerk at the request of the Applicant, Appellant or City’s staff.

COMMENTS BY THE CITY COMMISSION, CITY ATTORNEY & CITY MANAGER

minutes_note:
Thank You
Commissioner Biederman stated that Department of Public Works is one of the most impressive departments in the City, and requests submitted through Hollywood Connect are consistently addressed within days.
Boulevard Heights
Commissioner Biederman stated the State legislative funding secured for the Boulevard Heights Community Center Senior Program Expansion is something he has been working toward for several years. He thanked Marie Woodson, State Representative, for continuing to fight for the District.
title: Commissioner Biederman, District 5

minutes_note:
Story Time in the Park
Commissioner Quintana announced District 6 Summer Story Time in the Park series has concluded and will resume after daylight saving time ends. She stated Brian Rodriguez, Police Officer, deserves recognition for actively participating in the events rather than simply observing.
Donations for Colombia
Commissioner Quintana stated she is grateful to Hollywood Fire Rescue for collecting donations for earthquake relief in Colombia at all City Fire Stations.
7 Skies Park
Commissioner Quintana requested Commission support to name the small park that emerged from the State Road 7/441 road-widening project at Glen Parkway and Johnson Street “7 Skies Park”. She requested the formal naming process be waived as a Commission initiated action. Commissioner Quintana stated the name reflects the open skies visible from the site and aligns with the existing State Road 7/441 branding. All members of the Commission supported the idea.
title: Commissioner Quintana, District 6

minutes_note:
Thank you
Commissioner Shuham stated she agrees with Commissioner Biederman's praise of the Department of Public Works and thanked Joseph Kroll, Director of Public Works, for his team's responsiveness.
Agenda
Commissioner Shuham stated September 8, 2026, Planning and Development Board agenda was significantly overloaded for volunteer board members. She requested Commission support to give the beach overlay its own separate hearing night.
Election Campaign
Commissioner Shuham stated she is very grateful for the outcome of her County Commission race. She thanked the many volunteers and donors who supported her two-year campaign, and congratulated other candidates who ran positive campaigns. Commissioner Shuham stated she intends to bring the same inclusive approach to all District 6 constituents regardless of whether they voted for her or not. She recognized outgoing County Commissioner Beam Furr for his 24 years of combined service.
title: Commissioner Shuham, District 1

minutes_note:
Thank you
Commissioner Hernandez announced his appreciation for all City departments and Raelin Storey, City Manager, for all their work during the summer recess.
Street Lighting
Commissioner Hernandez stated the new streetlights along Fillmore Street east of the railroad tracks are now activated. He requested that lighting improvements also be prioritized along the south side of Hollywood Boulevard.
Littering
Commissioner Hernandez stated the small lot on State Road 7/441 and Hollywood Boulevard has been a site for trash dumping by passing motorists and requested the Police Department increase enforcement against littering. He stated the City should consider what long-term use visible lots serve.
Speed Tables
Commissioner Hernandez stated residents along 24th Avenue, south side of Washington Street to Pembroke Road have been requesting traffic calming measures for seven to ten years. He requested staff to prioritize that corridor.
Hispanic Heritage Month
Commissioner Hernandez announced the Hispanic Heritage Month celebration in Downtown Hollywood is scheduled for October 10, 2026. He encouraged Commission and community members to consider sponsoring the event through the Hispanic Affairs Council.
title: Commissioner Hernandez, District 2

minutes_note:
Rotary Park
Vice Mayor Callari stated during the morning Budget workshop, the Commission supports allocating additional funds if needed, to complete the Rotary Park Improvement Project. She requested staff bring back a full cost estimate as part of the capital budget process.
Stan Goldman Field
Vice Mayor Callari stated a community meeting will be scheduled soon regarding parking changes at Stan Goldman Field. She stated this is in response to numerous complaints she has received.
Tax Reform
Vice Mayor Callari stated the potential passage of Amendment 3 in November should prompt the City to begin researching annexation possibilities. She stated some smaller surrounding municipalities may face financial difficulty if property tax reform passes.
Advertising Meetings
Vice Mayor Callari stated outreach events held for the beach overlay project date, dating back to March, were held during the process, with two additional public open houses held in August. Vice Mayor Callari stated she is not in favor of delaying the items.
Community Member
Vice Mayor Callari stated she was pleased by the respectful tone of a recent letter received from a community member regarding the overlay and expressed hope that common ground can continue to be found.
Marine Biology Center
Vice Mayor Callari stated she has been asked to set up a meeting with Nova Southeastern University regarding the Marine Biology Center in the park. She stated this includes signage and potential partnership opportunities.
Flooding
Vice Mayor Callari stated flooding on Lincoln Road near 29th Avenue and I-95 is a long-standing concern. She stated she would like staff to evaluate the connection with the stormwater plan.
title: Vice Mayor Callari, District 3

minutes_note:
Thank you
Commissioner Gruber stated he wanted to thank staff, the Police Department, Fire Department, and the Fraternal Order of Police for donating ice cream at a recent community ice cream social, which he stated was one of the best-attended events he has participated in. He stated 400 ice creams were given out and interactive demonstrations by the Fire and Police Departments that included canine and SWAT units.
Parking
Commissioner Gruber stated he would like the Commission and staff to consider a pilot program of free parking in the Downtown garages on weekdays, particularly during the typically slow month of September, to test whether parking costs are a meaningful factor in Downtown foot traffic. He stated that pairing free or reduced garage parking with the Dine Out Hollywood initiative in October may be the most effective way to evaluate the impact.
Golf Course
Commissioner Gruber stated he believes the City should look into options for homeowners who live along golf courses and wish to install protective structures such as canopies or pergolas. He stated the process should be simplified and requested staff bring back options for an Ordinance applicable Citywide.
title: Commissioner Gruber, District 4

minutes_note:
Speed Tables
Mayor Levy stated he would like to make Commissioners aware that the speed table designs installed through the GO Bond have been widely criticized as too harsh and steep, requiring drivers to slow down well below the speed limit to traverse them comfortably. He stated older speed tables installed in the City, such as those on 28th Avenue, roll more smoothly. Mayor Levy stated that he believes any future speed tables need to feature a different product or design.
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated that recent drainage requirements have made the edges of new tables more abrupt and acknowledged the feedback.
Ribbon Cutting
Mayor Levy announced the ribbon cutting and public opening of the Hollywood Police Department's new headquarters at 401 North Park Road at 4:00 PM on Thursday, August 27, 2026. He stated parking is accessible via Entrada Drive.
title: Mayor Levy

minutes_note:
New Attorneys
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, announced two new attorneys to the Commission. She stated Farosha Andasheva, Senior Assistant City Attorney, who previously served as a legislative attorney for the City of Miami Beach for eight years, has joined the office and will be working primarily with the Development Services team.
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, announced Amy Drever, Public Safety Legal Advisor, who most recently served at the Broward Office of the Inspector General and previously spent nine years as a Miami-Dade prosecutor, has also joined the office and will be supporting the Police, Fire, Code, and Parking Departments.
title: City Attorney

minutes_note:
Donation
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated that she wanted to highlight several important items from the Consent Agenda, including a $139,500.00 donation of law enforcement forfeiture funds to support nonprofits such as the Boys and Girls Club, PAL, and Hispanic Unity, and the Highland Gardens Sidewalk Project funded through a $722,000.00 Florida Department of Transportation grant.
Budget Hearings
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced three upcoming community budget meetings: September 1, 2026, at the Hollywood Beach Culture and Community Center, September 9, 2026, at City Hall, and September 10, 2026, at the Boulevard Heights Community Center, all at 6:00 PM.
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated formal budget hearings will be held at City Hall at 6:00 PM on Monday, September 14, 2026, and Wednesday, September 23, 2026, then immediately followed by the CRA budget hearing.
Earthquake Relief
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated Hollywood Fire Rescue continues to collect supplies for Colombia earthquake relief at all fire stations and directed residents to the City website for a list of priority needs.
Telly Awards
Raelin Storey, City Manager, announced the Office of Communications, Marketing and Economic Development team won four Telly Awards, two silver and two bronze for the Aerospace Economic Development Commercial, the Fire recruitment video, and the Centennial Celebration.
Letter
Raelin Storey, City Manager, received a positive letter from a resident praising Lucas Kelly, Utilities Supervisor, for his professionalism in resolving water quality concerns. She stated that this serves as an important reminder of the high level of performance that City staff regularly display.
title: City Manager

Citizens' Comments shall be held on the First and Third Wednesday of each month at the Regular City Commission Meeting in the City Commission Chambers, Room 219, at 5:00 PM.

City Attorney Concern
Commissioner Hernandez stated he had concerns regarding the performance of Damaris Henlon, City Attorney. He stated that some residents he represents had brought concerns to his attention. Commissioner Hernandez questioned whether Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, had pursued the required continuing legal education credits toward her Florida Bar municipal law certification.
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, stated that she is currently enrolled in the necessary Continuing Learning Education and expects to be eligible to sit for the certification exam the following year.
Commissioner Hernandez requested proactive communication from Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, regarding her progress on such prerequisites would be appreciated. He stated his intent was not personal, but to act on constituent feedback and provide the Commission with an opportunity to discuss the matter.
Commissioner Biederman stated that no staff member or Commissioner is perfect. He stated he appreciated Ms. Henlon’s willingness to acknowledge the limits of her expertise and seeking outside counsel. Commissioner Biederman stated the $275,000 outside counsel budget is a worthwhile investment in getting results.
Commissioner Quintana stated the City Attorney has been experiencing a lot of changes recently and understands what is at stake, to make sure the highest level of expertise is on a particularly challenging legal issue instead of pretending to know more than they do.
Vice Mayor Callari stated she had concerns even at the time of the City Attorney's appointment, feeling the City required someone with more extensive municipal experience given its size and complexity. She stated she had heard concerns from staff, outside counsel, and other community partners, and urged the City Attorney to staff the department with more experienced attorneys.
Mayor Levy stated the annual performance review occurring at the end of the fiscal year was the appropriate formal venue for this discussion and encouraged Ms. Henlon to prepare a summary of major accomplishments and the status of key legal matters for that review. He stated he would welcome feedback from the City Manager's office on the responsiveness and performance of the City Attorney's office from a day to day departmental perspective.
Commissioner Shuham stated she felt uncomfortable with the way the subject was raised publicly without prior direct communication with the employee. She stated her strong support for the practice of seeking outside counsel on complex matters and cautioned that eliminating outside counsel to cut costs while also expecting in-house expertise on every issue is an unrealistic expectation. Commissioner Shuham stated the City faces a growing range of complicated legal challenges that no single in-house team could fully cover alone.
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, stated her appreciation for the feedback, acknowledged the increased volume and complexity of the City's legal workload. She explained the recruitment challenges of attracting experienced attorneys to government positions where salaries are significantly lower than private practice.
Damaris Henlon, City Attorney, stated she would address the feedback raised and welcomed individual meetings with each Commissioner.
Liquor License
Commissioner Hernandez stated there has been a rapid increase of 4:00 AM liquor licenses in the downtown area. He stated he had been approached by existing Downtown business owners and property owners who expressed concern about promoters bringing large crowds to venues, causing overflow affecting neighboring businesses and raised safety concerns. Commissioner Hernandez stated Hollywood currently has 13 active 4:00 AM licenses in Downtown. He suggested the Commission consider a moratorium on new 4:00 AM license applications while staff and public safety analyzed the issue.
Commissioner Biederman stated restricting new licenses while existing holders benefit from reduced competition raised fairness concerns and questioned whether enforcing existing laws and adding DUI checkpoints would be more appropriate than restricting licenses. He stated the discussion should also include the beach district.
Vice Mayor Callari stated she needed more data on DUI traffic stop statistics, Uber usage patterns, and information from the Downtown Business Association before supporting any change.
Commissioner Gruber requested data from the Police Department and a review of what competing Cities such as Fort Lauderdale and Miami permit before drawing conclusions. He stated that rolling back 4:00 AM licenses can significantly change the character of a City's nightlife.
Raelin Storey, City Manager, stated the conversation was being driven by existing Downtown stakeholders concerned about saturation, and confirmed that the current 4:00 AM license is a fully discretionary privilege that any qualifying applicant may receive. She stated staff would conduct a data-driven analysis and return to the Commission with findings and a recommendation.

QUASI-JUDICIAL HEARING PROCEDURES
AND RULES FOR EX-PARTE COMMUNICATIONS
I. Scope and Applicability. These procedures shall apply to all quasi-judicial hearings held by the City Commission or by any Board or Committee (hereinafter referred to as “Boards”) which holds quasi-judicial hearings. The City Attorney shall determine which matters are quasi-judicial in nature and shall direct the City Clerk or Board liaison to designate specially such matters on the agenda.
II. Proceedings. Mayor, Vice Mayor or other presiding officer (hereafter, the "Presiding Officer") shall conduct the proceedings and maintain order. The City Attorney or legal advisor shall represent the City Commission or Board, rule on all evidentiary and procedural issues and objections, and advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and necessary factual findings. Hearings shall be conducted informally, but with decorum. Formal rules of procedure shall not apply except as set forth herein; however, fundamental due process shall be accorded.
III. Unauthorized Communications. In all quasi-judicial hearings, all rulings must be based only upon the evidence presented at the hearing. In accordance with Section 286.0115(1), Florida Statutes, ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members in quasi-judicial matters is permissible and the adherence to the following procedures shall remove the presumption of prejudice arising from ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members:
1. The substance of any ex parte communication with a City Commissioner or Board member which relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board is not presumed prejudicial to the action if the subject of the communication and the identity of the person, group, or entity with whom the communication took place is disclosed and made a part of the record before the final action on the matter.
2. A City Commissioner or Board member may read a written communication from any person. However, a written communication that relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action, and such written communication shall be made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
3. City Commissioners or Board members may conduct investigations and site visits and may receive expert opinions regarding quasi-judicial action pending before them. Such activities shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action if the existence of the investigation, site visit, or expert opinion is made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
4. Disclosure made pursuant to subparagraphs 1, 2 and 3 must be made before or during the public meeting at which a vote is taken on such matters, so that persons who have opinions contrary to those expressed in the ex parte communication are give a reasonable opportunity to refute or respond to the communication.
IV. Witnesses and Supporting Materials. At least eight City business days before a quasi-judicial hearing.
A. Staff shall prepare a report, recommendation and supporting materials, a copy of which shall be available to the applicant, appellant and to the public at the City Clerk’s Office. Included in the supporting materials will be copies of all exhibits and documents upon which staff’s recommendation is based.
B. The Applicant and the Appellant, if applicable, shall submit a detailed outline of the argument in support of their application, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify in support of the application (including resumes for any witness the party intends to qualify as an expert).
C. The eight City business day deadline is necessary to ensure the Commission or Board members are given sufficient opportunity to review the written submissions prior to the hearing, and shall be strictly observed. Should the eight day City business day deadline be missed by either staff or the Applicant, the item may be continued at the discretion of the City Commission or Board to the next available agenda.
V. Party Intervenors. The City Attorney may allow a person to intervene as a Party Intervenor if they meet the following requirements:
A. The person must have an interest in the application, which is different than the public at large.
B. At least three days prior to the hearing, the person shall submit a written request to intervene including: a detailed outline of their interest in the application and argument in favor or against it, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at the hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify on their behalf (including resumes for any witness the person intends to qualify as an expert).
VI. Conduct of Hearing.
A. The Presiding Officer shall call the proceeding to order and announce that the hearing has begun.
B. The Presiding Officer, City Attorney or legal advisor shall inquire whether all parties, members of the public and Commission or Board members agree to waiving the quasi-judicial hearing.
C. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Attorney, legal advisor or Presiding Officer shall explain the rules concerning procedure, testimony, and admission of evidence.
D. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Clerk or staff liaison shall swear in all witnesses who are to testify at the hearing.
E. The order of proof shall be as follows:
1. A representative of the City’s staff (or outside counsel) shall briefly describe the Applicant’s request, introduce and review all relevant exhibits and evidence, report staff’s recommendation, and present any testimony in support of staff’s recommendation. Staff shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make their full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
2. The Appellant, if applicable, (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Appellant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make its full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
3. Any Party Intervenor (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of or opposed to the application. A Party Intervenor shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board Member.
4. The Applicant (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Applicant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
5. Any other persons present who wish to submit relevant information to the City Commission or Board shall speak next for a maximum of three minutes each (excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member). Members of the public will be permitted to present their non-expert opinions, but the Commission or board will be expressly advised that public sentiment is not relevant to the decision, which must be based only upon competent and substantial evidence.
6. The Appellant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
7. The Applicant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
8. The Party Intervenor will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
9. The City’s staff will make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
10. At the discretion of the Presiding Officer, the Applicant may be permitted to respond to the final Party Intervenor and staff comments and recommendations (maximum of three minutes).
G. The City Attorney or legal advisor will advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and the factual findings that must be made to approve or deny the application.
H. The City Commission or Board will conduct open deliberation of the application. The Presiding Officer shall have the discretion to reopen the proceeding for additional testimony or argument by the parties when an outcome substantially different than either the granting or denial of the application is being considered. After deliberations, a vote shall be taken to approve, approve with conditions or deny the application.
VII. Examination by Commissioners and City Attorney or Legal Advisor. Commissioners, Board members and the City Attorney or Legal Advisor may ask questions of persons presenting testimony or evidence at any time during the proceedings until commencement of deliberation.
VIII. Cross-Examination of Witnesses. After each witness testifies, the City staff representative, the Applicant’s representative, Appellant’s representative, and/or the Party Intervenor’s representative shall be permitted to question the witness, but such cross-examination shall be limited to matters about which the witness testified and shall be limited to five minutes per side. Members of the public will not be permitted to cross-examine witnesses. Cross-examination shall be permitted only as would be permitted in a Florida court of law.
IX. Rules of Evidence.
A. All evidence of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs shall be admissible, whether or not such evidence would be admissible in a court of law in Florida. Irrelevant, immaterial, harassing, defamatory or unduly repetitive evidence shall be excluded.
B. Hearsay evidence may be used for the purposes of supplementing or explaining other evidence, but it shall not be sufficient by itself to support a finding unless it would be admissible over objection in a civil action.
C. Documentary evidence may be presented in the form of a copy or the original. Upon request, parties shall be given an opportunity to compare the copy with the original.
X. Statements of Counsel. Statements of counsel, or any non-attorney representative, shall only be considered as argument and not testimony unless counsel or the representative is sworn in and the testimony if based on actual personal knowledge of the matters which are the subject of the statements.
XI. Continuances and Deferrals. The City Commission or Board shall consider requests for continuances made by City staff, the Applicant, the Appellant or a Party Intervenor and may grant continuances in its sole discretion. If, in the opinion of the City Commission or Board, any testimony or documentary evidence or information presented at the hearing justifies allowing additional research or review in order to properly determine the issue presented, then the City Commission or Board may continue the matter to a time certain to allow for such research or review.
XII. Transcription of hearing.
A. The City Clerk or staff liaison shall preserve the official transcript of the hearing through tape recording and/or video recording.
B. the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may arrange, at its own expense, for a court reporter to transcribe the hearing.
C. The Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may request that all or a part of the transcript of a hearing be transcribed into verbatim, written form. In such case, the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor requesting the transcript shall be responsible for the cost of production of the transcription and the transcription shall become the official transcript.
XIII. Maintenance of Evidence and Other Documents. The Office of the City Clerk or staff liaison shall retain all of the evidence and documents presented at the hearing unless any such evidence is too large to be stored by the City Clerk or staff liaison. In that event, such evidence will be stored in the Community Planning and Development Department.
XIV. False Testimony. Any willful false swearing on the part of any witness or person giving evidence before the Commission or Board as to any material fact in the proceedings shall be deemed to be perjury and shall be punished in the manner prescribed by law for such offense.
XV. Failure of Applicant to Appear. If the Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or their representative fails to appear at the time fixed for the hearing, and such absence is not excused by the Commission or Board, the Commission or Board may proceed to hear the evidence and render a decision thereon in absentia.
XVI. Subpoena Power. The Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or City’s staff shall be entitled to compel the attendance of witnesses through the use of subpoenas. All such subpoenas shall be issued by the City Clerk at the request of the Applicant, Appellant or City’s staff.
R-2016-334, 11/2/2016

The Regular City Commission Meeting of the City of Hollywood, Florida, was called to order by Mayor Levy on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 1:25 PM in the City Commission Room, Room 219, 2600 Hollywood Blvd., Hollywood, Florida.

As a courtesy the City is offering a new option for Citizens’ Comments, other than in-person comments, for persons to participate at 5:00 PM by telephone. The option for public comment via telephone is not available for Proclamations, Presentations or other agenda items. There shall be no duplication of issues that were heard on specifically agendaed items.
Advance registration is required to participate via telephone for Citizens' Comments at :
https://fl-hollywood2.civicplus.com/FormCenter/City-Clerk-12/Citizens-Comments-Telephone-Registration-291
This registration form must be received by noon on the Tuesday prior to the meeting. Requests received after this time will not be honored. The public is encouraged to participate in -person at City Hall, 2600 Hollywood Boulevard, room 219.
The Consent Agenda is comprised of items prepared by various offices and departments in the City. These items are routine and/or non-controversial in nature, and may be voted upon by the Commission in one motion as listed below.
The Regular agenda consists of items that must be discussed or that could be considered controversial, and are voted upon by the Commission individually.
Agenda items not scheduled for a specific time may be considered at any time during the meeting, at the Commission’s discretion. However, time certain items will not be considered by the Commission earlier than the time listed for those items, although those items may be taken up at a later time.
The following items on this agenda are time certain items.

The City of Hollywood is conducting its City Commission Meetings in person at City Hall, located at 2600 Hollywood Boulevard. To view the meeting agenda, please visit hollywoodfl .org. Members of the public may watch the City Commission Meetings via the City’s website at hollywoodfl.org/WatchMeeting, via livestream on the City’s YouTube Channel, on Comcast Channel 78 or ATT U-Verse Channel 99.
Any person who wishes to speak must first complete a comment card from the City Clerk. Comment cards must be returned to the City Clerk within the first five minutes after the start of the agenda item. After being recognized, approach the podium, give your name and address, identify your client or clients (if applicable). A citizen's time is not transferable to any other person.
Citizens' Comments shall be held on the First and Third Wednesday of each month at the Regular City Commission Meeting in the City Commission Chambers, Room 219, at 5:00 PM.
Lobbyist registration is required if any person, firm or corporation is lobbying the City Commission on any petition or issue, pursuant to the Section 30.15 of the Code of Ordinances.
Any person wishing to appeal any decision made by this Commission with respect to any matter considered at such meeting or hearing will need a record of the proceedings, and for such purposes may need to ensure that a verbatim record of the proceedings is made, which record includes the testimony and evidence upon which the appeal is made.
Two or more members of the same city board, commission, or committee, who are not of this Commission, may attend this meeting and may, at that time, discuss matters on which foreseeable action may later be taken by their board, commission or committee.
Persons with disabilities who require reasonable accommodations to participate in City programs and/or services may call the Clarissa Ip, ADA Coordinator/City Engineer, five business days in advance at 954-921-3915 (voice) or email: cip@hollywoodfl.org. If an individual is hearing or speech impaired, please call 1-800-955-8771 (V-TDD).
Disclosure of Real Estate Interests and Business Relationships - When an agenda item involves the use or development of land, each member of the City Commission, City Manager, Assistant City Manager(s), City Attorney, Deputy City Attorney, and the director and assistant director (s) of each City department/office shall disclose orally, at the time the City Commission begins to discuss the item, or in writing to the City Clerk prior to the publication of the agenda, any significant interest (as defined below) that such City official or employee or any relative of such City official or employee has in land located within 300 feet of the land that is the subject of the item. When an agenda item involves an invitation for bids, request for proposals, request for qualifications, request for letters of interest, or other competitive solicitation, each member of the City Commission, City Manager, Assistant City Manager(s), City Attorney, Deputy City Attorney, and the director and assistant director (s) of each City department/office shall disclose orally, at the time the City Commission begins to discuss the item, or in writing to the City Clerk prior to the publication of the agenda, any client or business relationship that such City official or employee or any relative of such City official or employee has with any business entity that has submitted a response to the competitive solicitation. “Significant interest” means ownership of more than five percent of the value of the land.
Persons attending meetings shall remain seated at all times unless called upon to speak, will not call out comments during the meeting or make inappropriate hand or facial gestures. Please silence all cell phones prior to entering the meeting.

QUASI-JUDICIAL HEARING PROCEDURES
AND RULES FOR EX-PARTE COMMUNICATIONS
I. Scope and Applicability. These procedures shall apply to all quasi-judicial hearings held by the City Commission or by any Board or Committee (hereinafter referred to as “Boards”) which holds quasi-judicial hearings. The City Attorney shall determine which matters are quasi-judicial in nature and shall direct the City Clerk or Board liaison to designate specially such matters on the agenda.
II. Proceedings. Mayor, Vice Mayor or other presiding officer (hereafter, the "Presiding Officer") shall conduct the proceedings and maintain order. The City Attorney or legal advisor shall represent the City Commission or Board, rule on all evidentiary and procedural issues and objections, and advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and necessary factual findings. Hearings shall be conducted informally, but with decorum. Formal rules of procedure shall not apply except as set forth herein; however, fundamental due process shall be accorded.
III. Unauthorized Communications. In all quasi-judicial hearings, all rulings must be based only upon the evidence presented at the hearing. In accordance with Section 286.0115(1), Florida Statutes, ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members in quasi-judicial matters is permissible and the adherence to the following procedures shall remove the presumption of prejudice arising from ex parte communications with City Commissioners or Board members:
1. The substance of any ex parte communication with a City Commissioner or Board member which relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board is not presumed prejudicial to the action if the subject of the communication and the identity of the person, group, or entity with whom the communication took place is disclosed and made a part of the record before the final action on the matter.
2. A City Commissioner or Board member may read a written communication from any person. However, a written communication that relates to a quasi-judicial action pending before the Commission or Board shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action, and such written communication shall be made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
3. City Commissioners or Board members may conduct investigations and site visits and may receive expert opinions regarding quasi-judicial action pending before them. Such activities shall not be presumed prejudicial to the action if the existence of the investigation, site visit, or expert opinion is made a part of the record before final action on the matter.
4. Disclosure made pursuant to subparagraphs 1, 2 and 3 must be made before or during the public meeting at which a vote is taken on such matters, so that persons who have opinions contrary to those expressed in the ex parte communication are give a reasonable opportunity to refute or respond to the communication.
IV. Witnesses and Supporting Materials. At least eight City business days before a quasi-judicial hearing.
A. Staff shall prepare a report, recommendation and supporting materials, a copy of which shall be available to the applicant, appellant and to the public at the City Clerk’s Office. Included in the supporting materials will be copies of all exhibits and documents upon which staff’s recommendation is based.
B. The Applicant and the Appellant, if applicable, shall submit a detailed outline of the argument in support of their application, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify in support of the application (including resumes for any witness the party intends to qualify as an expert).
C. The eight City business day deadline is necessary to ensure the Commission or Board members are given sufficient opportunity to review the written submissions prior to the hearing, and shall be strictly observed. Should the eight day City business day deadline be missed by either staff or the Applicant, the item may be continued at the discretion of the City Commission or Board to the next available agenda.
V. Party Intervenors. The City Attorney may allow a person to intervene as a Party Intervenor if they meet the following requirements:
A. The person must have an interest in the application, which is different than the public at large.
B. At least three days prior to the hearing, the person shall submit a written request to intervene including: a detailed outline of their interest in the application and argument in favor or against it, copies of all exhibits which will be presented at the hearing and the names and addresses of all witnesses who will be called to testify on their behalf (including resumes for any witness the person intends to qualify as an expert).
VI. Conduct of Hearing.
A. The Presiding Officer shall call the proceeding to order and announce that the hearing has begun.
B. The Presiding Officer, City Attorney or legal advisor shall inquire whether all parties, members of the public and Commission or Board members agree to waiving the quasi-judicial hearing.
C. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Attorney, legal advisor or Presiding Officer shall explain the rules concerning procedure, testimony, and admission of evidence.
D. When the quasi-judicial hearing is not waived, the City Clerk or staff liaison shall swear in all witnesses who are to testify at the hearing.
E. The order of proof shall be as follows:
1. A representative of the City’s staff (or outside counsel) shall briefly describe the Applicant’s request, introduce and review all relevant exhibits and evidence, report staff’s recommendation, and present any testimony in support of staff’s recommendation. Staff shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make their full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
2. The Appellant, if applicable, (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Appellant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make its full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
3. Any Party Intervenor (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of or opposed to the application. A Party Intervenor shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board Member.
4. The Applicant (or his/her representative or counsel) shall present evidence and testimony in support of the application. Applicant shall have a maximum of 30 minutes to make his/her full presentation, including opening statement and all direct presentation by witnesses, but excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member.
5. Any other persons present who wish to submit relevant information to the City Commission or Board shall speak next for a maximum of three minutes each (excluding any cross-examination or questions from the Commission or a Board member). Members of the public will be permitted to present their non-expert opinions, but the Commission or board will be expressly advised that public sentiment is not relevant to the decision, which must be based only upon competent and substantial evidence.
6. The Appellant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
7. The Applicant will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
8. The Party Intervenor will be permitted to make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
9. The City’s staff will make final comments, if any (maximum of five minutes).
10. At the discretion of the Presiding Officer, the Applicant may be permitted to respond to the final Party Intervenor and staff comments and recommendations (maximum of three minutes).
G. The City Attorney or legal advisor will advise the City Commission or Board as to the applicable law and the factual findings that must be made to approve or deny the application.
H. The City Commission or Board will conduct open deliberation of the application. The Presiding Officer shall have the discretion to reopen the proceeding for additional testimony or argument by the parties when an outcome substantially different than either the granting or denial of the application is being considered. After deliberations, a vote shall be taken to approve, approve with conditions or deny the application.
VII. Examination by Commissioners and City Attorney or Legal Advisor. Commissioners, Board members and the City Attorney or Legal Advisor may ask questions of persons presenting testimony or evidence at any time during the proceedings until commencement of deliberation.
VIII. Cross-Examination of Witnesses. After each witness testifies, the City staff representative, the Applicant’s representative, Appellant’s representative, and/or the Party Intervenor’s representative shall be permitted to question the witness, but such cross-examination shall be limited to matters about which the witness testified and shall be limited to five minutes per side. Members of the public will not be permitted to cross-examine witnesses. Cross-examination shall be permitted only as would be permitted in a Florida court of law.
IX. Rules of Evidence.
A. All evidence of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs shall be admissible, whether or not such evidence would be admissible in a court of law in Florida. Irrelevant, immaterial, harassing, defamatory or unduly repetitive evidence shall be excluded.
B. Hearsay evidence may be used for the purposes of supplementing or explaining other evidence, but it shall not be sufficient by itself to support a finding unless it would be admissible over objection in a civil action.
C. Documentary evidence may be presented in the form of a copy or the original. Upon request, parties shall be given an opportunity to compare the copy with the original.
X. Statements of Counsel. Statements of counsel, or any non-attorney representative, shall only be considered as argument and not testimony unless counsel or the representative is sworn in and the testimony if based on actual personal knowledge of the matters which are the subject of the statements.
XI. Continuances and Deferrals. The City Commission or Board shall consider requests for continuances made by City staff, the Applicant, the Appellant or a Party Intervenor and may grant continuances in its sole discretion. If, in the opinion of the City Commission or Board, any testimony or documentary evidence or information presented at the hearing justifies allowing additional research or review in order to properly determine the issue presented, then the City Commission or Board may continue the matter to a time certain to allow for such research or review.
XII. Transcription of hearing.
A. The City Clerk or staff liaison shall preserve the official transcript of the hearing through tape recording and/or video recording.
B. the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may arrange, at its own expense, for a court reporter to transcribe the hearing.
C. The Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor may request that all or a part of the transcript of a hearing be transcribed into verbatim, written form. In such case, the Applicant, Appellant or Party Intervenor requesting the transcript shall be responsible for the cost of production of the transcription and the transcription shall become the official transcript.
XIII. Maintenance of Evidence and Other Documents. The Office of the City Clerk or staff liaison shall retain all of the evidence and documents presented at the hearing unless any such evidence is too large to be stored by the City Clerk or staff liaison. In that event, such evidence will be stored in the Community Planning and Development Department.
XIV. False Testimony. Any willful false swearing on the part of any witness or person giving evidence before the Commission or Board as to any material fact in the proceedings shall be deemed to be perjury and shall be punished in the manner prescribed by law for such offense.
XV. Failure of Applicant to Appear. If the Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or their representative fails to appear at the time fixed for the hearing, and such absence is not excused by the Commission or Board, the Commission or Board may proceed to hear the evidence and render a decision thereon in absentia.
XVI. Subpoena Power. The Applicant, the Appellant or Party Intervenor or City’s staff shall be entitled to compel the attendance of witnesses through the use of subpoenas. All such subpoenas shall be issued by the City Clerk at the request of the Applicant, Appellant or City’s staff.
